body.text: At the market you may buy half a kilogram of sugar, 0.5 litres of cooking oil, or a dress with 20% off. A half, 0.5 and 50% are three ways of writing the same amount. This topic shows how fractions, decimals and percentages are linked.
Types of fractions
A fraction shows part of a whole. The bottom number, the denominator, tells how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The top number, the numerator, tells how many parts we take.

items: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, such as 3/4.
An improper fraction has a numerator equal to or bigger than its denominator, such as 7/4.
A mixed number is a whole number and a proper fraction together, such as 1 3/4.
Equivalent fractions have the same value, such as 1/2 = 2/4 = 5/10.

body.text: Improper fractions and mixed numbers

To change an improper fraction to a mixed number, divide the numerator by the denominator. The remainder becomes the new numerator. To go back, multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator.
Fractions in real life
To add or subtract fractions, first write them with the same denominator.

body.text: Working with decimals
A decimal is a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. So 0.7 = 7/10 and 0.25 = 25/100. When adding or subtracting decimals, line up the decimal points.

To multiply decimals, multiply as whole numbers. Then count the decimal places in both numbers and give the answer that many places. To divide by a decimal, multiply both numbers by 10, 100 or more until you divide by a whole number.

body.title: Four operations with decimals
steps: Multiply: 1.2 × 0.3. First 12 × 3 = 36. There are two decimal places in total, so the answer is 0.36.
Divide: 4.5 ÷ 0.15. Multiply both by 100 to get 450 ÷ 15 = 30.

body.text: Fractions and decimals
To change a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. To change a decimal to a fraction, write it over 10, 100 or 1,000, then simplify.
Kinds of decimals

items: A terminating decimal stops, such as 1/4 = 0.25.
A recurring decimal repeats a digit or group of digits forever, such as 1/3 = 0.333… and 2/11 = 0.1818…
A non-terminating, non-recurring decimal goes on forever with no repeating pattern, such as π = 3.14159…

body.text: We show a recurring decimal with a dot over the repeating digit. So 0.333… is written 0.3 with a dot over the 3.
Recurring decimals as fractions
Call the decimal x. Multiply by 10 if one digit repeats, or by 100 if two digits repeat. Subtract to remove the repeating part.

body.title: Write 0.444… and 0.2727… as fractions
steps: Let y = 0.2727… Two digits repeat, so 100y = 27.2727…

body.speech: ten x minus x equals four point four four four recurring minus nought point four four four recurring, so nine x equals four

body.text: Percentages
Per cent means "out of 100". A percentage is a fraction with denominator 100. To change a fraction or decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100%. To change a percentage back, divide by 100.

body.speech: percentage of a quantity equals the percentage over one hundred, times the quantity

body.text: Percentages in real life

body.title: Comparing two days of sales
steps: A trader in Owino market sells 21 of her 25 bunches of matooke on Monday and 31 of 40 bunches on Tuesday. On which day did she sell a bigger share?
She sold a bigger share on Monday, even though she sold more bunches on Tuesday.

body.title: Discounts and price rises
steps: A pair of shoes costs UGX 40,000. The shop gives 15% off.
The price of a bunch of matooke rises from UGX 20,000 to UGX 25,000.

body.title: Fold the fractions
body.text: Take four strips of paper of the same length. Leave one whole. Fold one in half, one in quarters and one in eighths. Label each part as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage. Line the strips up to find fractions that are equal, such as 2/4 and 4/8.
Use a calculator to change 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, 1/7 and 1/8 into decimals. Which ones stop and which ones repeat? Look at the denominators. Can you see a pattern?

Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways of writing the same amount. To find a percentage of a quantity, divide by 100 and multiply by the percentage. A recurring decimal can always be written as a fraction.
